s: Chíikoin meran jíkiketianra báke kóiman joín rétemakeanke.
e: The child nearly suffocated from getting into the middle of the smoke.
Grandpa's eyesight is blurry all over.

s: Yamébi koínkoin kéotaronki mawákanon róati íkai.
e: They say that when the vaca-muchacho sings at night, it is a bad omen; it is a sign that someone is going to die.

s: Moa kóinaxa kikínbires ícha ói máanke.
e: After it clouded over, a great deal of rain fell.

s: Papán jawen wái ménoara ochóxonbi óina koíwanke.
e: When we looked this morning from afar at the field papa had burned, it was smoking.

s: Jawen bákebo koíranai ikaxa átapa sináke.
e: The hen gets fierce to protect her chicks.

s: Sánjoan níwe pakéketianra mánkoa poyan páketi koíshike.
e: When the San Juan wind came, mango branches fell and made a loud crash.

s: En poróto bánakenbira ea kóitatasan ea píanaanke.
e: The tingoteros ate all the beans I had planted.
My maternal uncle went off to the army to become a soldier.
In the Sipiría stream there are many *kokáiki isáni* birds.

s: Néno jakatiíbira nato jóni moa kokámebo xaran káa iki, jawen ánibo mawáketian.
e: This man lived here a long time ago, but he went to live among the Cocamas because his parents died.
The chick died from swallowing a large cockroach.

s: Jawen kóko betanra Káte keó akí kake.
e: Cate went to gather caimitillo fruits with his nephew.

s: Nokon kókobakera Ikítoain káke sontáro jíkii.
e: My dear nephew went to Iquitos to join the army.
I ate two watermelons with no help.

s: Nato bími kokó ikénbira en títa ménike, onányamaxon.
e: Without realizing it, I gave mama a fruit that had already been eaten.

s: Jatíribi bímibora kókoa bátashaman iki; jatíribi páe iki.
e: Some fruits, when sucked, are very sweet; and others are very sour.

s: Káchio kóma bénai káketianronki jóniki inón bínike.
e: They tell that once a man went to look for a panguana in the forest, and the jaguar carried him off.

s: Jawen kóma jaíba meráketianra, aínbaon átapa réteke.
e: The woman killed a hen to feed her comadre who had visited her.
The truth is difficult to know.
He is a bad man.

s: Moátianronki béskoman Inkán chíi tsisto boxón komán tanon rakánike.
e: They tell that in ancient times a little parrot carried the burning ember of the Inca and placed it in a dry shihuahuaco.
When the shihuahuaco *bárikoman* cutipas a small child, his belly swells; and afterward he gets diarrhea.
They say that when we feed yungururo to a child, he gets dysentery.
Papa went yesterday to the Tabacoa stream to get chambira.
They say that our Inca's money is in Kumaría.
My crossbow made of cumaceba has been stolen from me.

s: Nato bákera jáwe ikáxmabi kómeman kópia sión ikal.
e: This child cries out for no reason at all; he seems to be cutipado (afflicted with supernatural harm) by the *komén* tree.

s: Nato komíko niá namameara papán wáme réteke.
e: Beneath this trunk of the *komíko* shrub papa killed a paiche (a large fish).
At the festival a Campa put over his shoulder a bandolier made of *kómokomo* seeds.
The enraged river dolphin made the water bubble.

s: Níwanaitian jéne komón ikainra, westíora yoxánshoko ráketi siónsion ika iki.
e: A little old woman cried out in fear at seeing the water bubble when there was an earthquake.
The boy makes the water bubble by diving in.

s: Bakísha jawen kómpa betan ríkani kaíbake.
e: Yesterday he went fishing with his compadre.

s: Bákebaonra jaton kómpanyirobo yóyo ati iki.
e: The students are to converse with their classmates.

s: Chópakon chitóntira bási páyotai, jakónhakin aká.
e: A pampanilla (a woven wrap-skirt) woven of stiff cloth lasts a long time, as long as it is well woven.
Even though he watched carefully what was happening, his boss cheated him.
They say the *kónawe* bird can keep its gaze fixed on the sun all day long.
Dad invited them to drink very fermented masato.

s: Títashokonra jawen bába konésake, kóri sáwemati.
e: The grandmother pierced her granddaughter's lip to put an ornament on her.

s: Rókotoronra kóni piáx chíxotaitian ráo xéamake.
e: The doctor had him take a medicine when he had diarrhea from having eaten eel.

s: Aménwaka jónira kónibo xaran kásh wanóke.
e: An Amahuaca man went to live among the Konibo and married a woman of that group.

s: Nato jonínra koníjo kaiyai ixonbira pimayamai.
e: This man raises rabbits, but he doesn't feed them.

s: Konínewan xenín wiskíxonronki non jato pirótanin kanántiki.
e: They say that when we paint our legs with gymnotus fat, we can win at soccer.

s: Bákera jawen titán konjíti kókomakashamai, jawen xéta payóti iketian.
e: The mother forbids her child to eat candy, because it ruins the teeth.
They say the firefly demons are good hunters.
The *konkón* condor eats the white lagarto (a caiman).
They tell that long ago there was a man who ate only mushrooms.
When the wood of a tree rots, various mushrooms come out.

s: Konónbi máana kókoaitianra epán manánxawe ícha bíke.
e: My uncle, my father's brother, caught many motelos (tortoises) when they were eating *konónbi* fruits fallen from the tree.

s: Bákera konrón bíi néetaitian binán tékake.
e: When the boy was climbing to get inciras, a wasp stung him.
The curaca does not like to eat food prepared with guisador.
They say that when we eat conta seeds, we become lazy.
The grandfather shot the jaguar that was high up in the masha cedar.

s: Konxán xatera pápa jawen pátoronin bichínke.
e: The boss took away dad's piece of cedar.
The boil on the thigh discharged a lot of pus.
The pot is *tipping over.*
The canoe has tipped over.
Ant bites form pus in us.
When the boil was already full of pus, the doctor opened it with a scalpel.
Yesterday we went to the cocha (an oxbow lake) and ate *kopén.*

s: Kikínbires kopíora ikénbira nato átapanin noa mároke pikáshorai.
e: Even though it was too expensive, we bought this hen because we were hungry.

s: Jatíbi jawékira rama jawen kopí bebónyorabo iki.
e: Nowadays everything has excessively high prices.

s: Nokon átapanin mia yómetsoa kopira en mia ichátamashoko kopíai.
e: I am going to pay you less (for your work) because you have stolen my hen.

s: Westíora kirínkoninra píchika pácha waránka sóro ea ménike, jéma akínti kopi.
e: A foreigner gave me five hundred thousand soles to invest in community development.

s: Non pápabaonra ícha jawéki noa kopi aká iki.
e: Our parents have done many things for us.
Because of you I have ended up badly off.

s: Jawen pátoroninra kárasira meran níake, ishtón kopíayamaitian.
e: The boss put (the indebted employee) in jail because he did not soon pay what he owed.

s: Moa kárasira meran ákanabira kopíaax pikóke.
e: They put him in jail, but he got out by bribing.

s: Ochítininra báke natéxke; játianra kópikin ríshkike.
e: When the dog bit the boy, he gave it a beating.
When his enemy punched him, he knocked him out.

s: Nokon shínamanbi ménikinra en mia kopímabi méniai.
e: I give it to you free, because that is my will.

s: Nato pátoronra jakómaixon noa kopímabires konxán mároxonke.
e: This boss bought our timber at a very low price because he is very bad.

s: Nato chópara Máioshiainbi kopímatani iki; ríkatonin boára kopí iki.
e: In Pucallpa these cloths are somewhat cheap; but when the river trader takes them to sell, he marks them up a lot.
They say that when the lupuna (a Ceiba tree) cutipas a baby, its belly swells.

s: Ronón ewan báke kópiaronki jósho chíxotai.
e: When the boa cutipas the baby, it gets a yellowish diarrhea.
They say that when the cow cutipas a baby, it drools a lot.
They say that when we eat cupiso, we grow weak.

s: Pápara paránta korá xéakasi átsaxeatira akashamai.
e: Dad does not want to drink masato (a fermented drink), but rather chapo.

s: Barín koráa téri jámataxa báke wínike.
e: The child cried when he stepped on the pitch melted by the sun.

s: Moára non koráake nato ipó báchi.
e: We have already melted these carachama eggs.
The mother is softening plantains to make chapo.

s: Kakónkonia koráka íkasi jóni nótsiketianra ímakanke.
e: A man who wanted to be curaca of. Caco got so angry when they would not accept him that in the end they had to make him one.

s: Ipó báchi en biára moa koráke.
e: The carachama eggs I got have already melted.
The teacher punished them because they were making a lot of noise, talking inside the school.
This woman does not want to put an ornament in her lower lip.
They say the Son of the Inca came in a little canoe of gold.
Dad speared the capitari while it was eating guama (a fruit).

s: Pátoronbaonra noa koríki méniamakatitai; jawékiboresa noa ménikatitai.
e: Years ago the bosses did not pay us with money but only with goods.
Write down these sums of money.
Although I look for five-tenth coins, I cannot find them.
A thief carried off money made of brass when he got into the house.
They say the banknotes of the water demons are the scales of paiche (a large river fish).
They say that in the Jenepanshea stream there are silver mines.
Mom's pampanilla (a wrap skirt) is a striking gray color.
Church songs have choruses.
The turkey kicked the child until he started to scream.
The soldiers come playing their bugles.
The children will be in two groups.
What color is the plantain?
A man made a cross-shaped cut in his enemy's back with his machete.
The priest baptized the boy and gave him a crucifix.
According to the story, long ago they crucified Jesus Christ.
It was black, but it turned gray.
The doctor treats a child who has a gray spot on the eye.

s: Nato chópara nokon títana bebónbires kóshi iki.
e: This cloth is stronger than my mother's.
the sovereign God

s: Non koshín yóia jóibicho senénhaxonon akánwe.
e: Let us obey only the words of our leader.
Although he was weak, they trained him by making him run.
Shout to him loudly; otherwise, he won't hear you.
He has become strong from playing so much soccer.
He had fainted, but he is moving now.

s: Nato simánanin nontée anón akanwe, non ajíntiki kóshixon.
e: This week let's do the work depending on our agent.

s: Non ápora jóai; jáki kóshixon koríki yokánon akawen.
e: Our president is coming; let's have confidence in him and ask him for money.
When the motor (motorboat) turned sideways, it crashed into the palizada (a driftwood pile).
The drunken man smashed this *kósho* container of mom's.

s: Wétsabo áti shínanira yobé janbíx kóshomeeke.
e: The sorcerer bewitched himself by wanting to bewitch others.
They say that when the lobo marino (a sea lion) bewitches us, we feel pain all over the body.
They say the cushuri is the offspring of the water demons.
They say that when the bufeo bewitches us, we feel stomach pain.
My maternal uncle got many *koshpámparo* fish.

s: Oa jónira koshpánya iki, xoáyora ikáx.
e: That man has a dewlap because he is very fat.
The cook wasted the chicken broth.

s: Papán awínwetsan kotónra jéne meran káke.
e: Papa's sister-in-law's blouse fell into the water.

s: Jawen kótoman yómetsoai méraxonra koáratia keshánke.
e: When he saw that someone was stealing his shirt, he told a guard.

s: Nokon chái en átsaxeati kóxetabira ea xéaxonkashamake.
e: Although I offered my brother-in-law the masato (a fermented drink), he would not drink it.
**misbíton píke.** The cat ate the *kóxkochi* dove that mother raised.
As he expired, he gave a death rattle.
They say the *koxkóxtobi* dove sings exactly at noon to indicate the time.
Papa shot at the wild turkey, but missed.

s: Titán kóxónewa píketianra jawen báke chixóke.
e: The mother ate meat of the *kóxónewa* guan, and her little child got sick with diarrhea.
Yesterday I caught a motelo (a tortoise) while it was eating the fruits of the *kóxónxewa* tree.
They say that when the *kóxopeox* tree cutipa (afflicts magically) a child, its body turns black.
In the oxbow lake the tucunari fish get stunned.
The *koyénke* lizard is not venomous.
The little *kóyo* ants got into the tin of honey.
This child is afraid of the *kóyobocho* bird.
with dirt stuck on the head
skin of the crown of the head
short in stature
to search over the surface of the ground
to finish the ceiling
to roof up to the peak of a house
to reach the peak of a hill
to sew (a full sack) at the mouth
to paint (a paddle) with designs on the handle
to stand on top
to surpass, to go over

s: Nato jóni riki kikínbires yóitima bákema ikáxbi.
e: This man is very disobedient even though he is not a child.
The ocelot carried off the small chicken.

s: Rámara neténma ránsakanai; moara netén ípachokanai.
e: Now they no longer dance during the day; but before, they did.

s: Rámara ea Kakónkoma iki; moátianra ea jaín ikátiai.
e: I no longer live in Caco, but before I lived there.

s: Jato báimakin senénhaxonra en jato jíwi réramai.
e: When I make them finish opening the trail, I am going to make them fell trees to get lumber.
Show it to me.
Don't let the ocelot get into the henhouse.

s: Rókotoroiba bóyamaxonra maton, nato aínbo mawámakeanke.
e: If you all had not taken this woman to the doctor, you would have let her die.

s: Bóchiki ixon shinón shekésh máanhaara non kókoke.
e: We ate the charichuelas (a jungle fruit) that the monkey threw down from above.

s: Yóashiko Inkánronki chíi bikánketian jatoki ói máanhaka iki.
e: They say that Stingy Inca made it rain down on those who had stolen the fire.
I unload the things from the canoe.

s: Jaín wáka yámaaxbi máan iki kéotaira en ninkáke; yoshínra íbiral.
e: I heard something; it sounded to me like the mooing of a cow, but there wasn't one there; it must have been a demon.
Back then the demons fell from above.

s: Oi máanaitianra ea káyamake, moa néseken kanóx.
e: I stayed while the rain fell and waited until it calmed down.

s: Titán tóroaka mabánra, jawen babán ménonaanke.
e: Her grandson burned the warp that mom had made.

s: Papán táriaxonoxonra nokon wáatan yomán mabánkin péoke.
e: My aunt, my mother's sister, began to warp the thread to weave a cushma (traditional tunic) for dad.

s: Nokon bakénra min báke mabóchonin cháchike; atapa áti shinánkin.
e: By accident, my son stuck your child with a *mabócho* arrow while trying to hunt a chicken.
The traveling trader sells machetes to them at very high prices.
When she fell, she hit her head.

s: Káko jónibora kímishai jaton xóbo máeax, maekanke kétokan baitian.
e: The inhabitants of Caco moved house three times because of the riverbank collapse.
They say that when the huancahui sings, a person dies.

s: Táma bimi piáxonki jatíbi yápa wetsánko máeyamai.
e: They say that when the fish eat peanuts, they all stay and don't go to another lake.

s: Jenén jato mápoara, jaton jéma máekin potákanke.
e: They abandoned their community and relocated to another place because the flood covered them.

s: Nato báritianra jéne ícha bexón, jíshtima ítiakin mái mápoke.
e: This year we had a great flood and it covered the land until it disappeared.
Our homeland has three regions.

s: Main beten píi áshea ikásha ea atón pikáshamai.
e: I didn't like eating tuna because I was used to eating akarawasú porridge.
The bujurqui is edible.

s: Nato jóxokoriki míinkani biáxmain, noa yómetso íti iki.
e: It seems that if we take this nine-tenths coin that was buried long ago, we could end up being thieves.
He must have gone to Iquitos, right?
Nima is leaving, isn't he?
—Might your husband not have seen my son? —Yes; they say he did.

s: Oropampan kaíra noa maísbicho káa iki, já bóti yámaketian.
e: Heading to the Urubamba, we went without any food because there was nothing to bring.

s: En mia pímapananra ea maís iki.
e: I'm very sorry. I would feed you, but I have nothing.
Every day Pepe brought water to the teacher.

s: Nato báritianra Kakónkoniabo maístorooma íkanai, tiníntinin jato párana kopí.
e: This year the inhabitants of Caco have no teacher because the lieutenant governor deceived them.

s: En panyón máiketianra, ea jónibaon osánke.
e: When I put a kerchief on my head, people laughed at me.

s: Jaínra máitia jóni jóai; járiki non koráka.
e: There comes a man wearing a crown; he is our curaca (chief).

s: Nato jonínra máiti máikin jéneyamai mánkoya ixon.
e: This man always wears a hat because he is bald.

s: Nokon titánra móromaiti áti onánke, jawen titán áxeaa ixon.
e: My mother knows how to make bead crowns, because her mother taught her.

s: Jémanapon niáx máitaitianra pórisiabaon jóni paena bóke, xponóxon.
e: The town's police took away a drunk man, who was speaking violently in the middle of the public, to lock him in jail.

s: Eara rabé chónka báritiayaníx mákachipon píkota iki.
e: When I was twenty years old, a molar came in.

s: Moátianronki non rekén baonki mákaman pérakanxonki jawéki xóipaokanike.
e: They say that our ancestors used to cook food by placing it on stones in the heat of the sun.
Now the road is covered with gravel.
The child got bitten by a piranha while bathing.
They say the *makéntita* fish is the size of a paco (pacu fish).

s: Máki peira jakón iki ján xénoati.
e: The juice of the *máki* herb's leaves is good for treating siso (a skin ailment).

s: Titán kóchi bákera makín meran káx mawáke.
e: Mother's piglet went into a hole in the ground and died there.

s: Kikín kopíora riki chópa kéxeti mákina.
e: The sewing machine is very expensive.

s: Péokin mamánchi óinaxa báke sión inike, yoxínra íbirai ikax.
e: Upon seeing a nun for the first time, the child screamed, thinking she was a demon or a ghost.
The blind know things only by touching them.
**jawen bábabo mámepaske.** When he came from Lima, the grandfather laid his hands on the heads of his grandchildren.

s: Nato jóni mámpara sontáro káyamai, ánima ikax.
e: This dwarf cannot do military service because he is very short.

s: Enra mámpi píai; ixónbira en wétsa jawékibo áyamai ea chixónaketian.
e: I eat turtle-egg omelets, but very carefully, for fear that they will give me diarrhea.

s: Nawán kéenyora riki ja kabóri bachi mampín.
e: The taricaya egg omelet is highly prized by mestizos.

s: Titán mampínhakenbira jawen bakén píamai, chixónaketian.
e: Mom prepares turtle-egg omelets, but her son doesn't eat them because he fears they will give him diarrhea.
aguaje (a palm fruit)
He hit me with an aguaje fruit.

s: Jatíbi jawékibo mánaii sénénaxa ea joríbake.
e: After gazing at everything, I returned.
They say a demon screams from the peak of Canchahuaya Hill.

s: Mánamanronki wísoinobo ícha iki; jáinoaronki kampán westíora rétea iki.
e: They say there are many yanapumas (black panthers) in the hills, and that a Campa killed one.

s: Nato manán wínobaini katánwe; kaxónra min jaínoa nókoti iki, já mia kéenai jawéki.
e: Go on; past this rise you will find what you want.

s: Manánkawishpo ikáinra ábion pakéke; chósko chónka jónira keyóke.
e: A plane crashed on a long hill, and forty people died.

s: Sípiria meranra westíora jéma iki, manántenaman iká; tsónra já onányamake tsóa jóniborin ixon.
e: Inside Sipiría stream, on the slope of a hill, there is an unknown village, and nobody knows who its inhabitants are.
It is the tortoise that holds up the world.

s: Manánxawen tápitira, kikínbires jakón iki ján ochíti raónti; jatianra manánxawe ícha bíai.
e: The *manánxawen tápiti* vine is very good for treating a dog, and it also makes it catch many tortoises.
Three small planes are circling above Yarinacocha.
They say the Inca's house is on the edge of a cocha (oxbow lake).

s: Jóni jenén réteaitianra, mapéxon moa manáon akánke.
e: They pulled out the man who was drowning and set him on the bank.

s: Non róo mánapo piáronki noa kírika onáma íti iki.
e: They say that if we eat howler monkey brains, we become slow at reading anything.

s: Mánati ea yóiyabira, ea moa jóke, játsanax.
e: Although he told me to wait for him, I came back because I got bored.
The man they were waiting for has already arrived.

s: Wáka manchan wéxaxon xéaaronki róookon ítima iki.
e: They say that if you drink from a cow's horn shavings scraped from a cow's [horn], whooping cough is avoided.

s: Manchánronki yoshín iki; yobéjonin jóni réteti ráanai.
e: They say the *manchán* bird is a demon, and that the shaman sends it to kill people.

s: Nokon titánra átapa manchónya, ríkaton namánbires máromake.
e: My mother sold a chicken with feather tufts to a traveling trader for a very low price.

s: Chomón xéati máneti shinánkinra bakén chómo tóeke.
e: The girl broke the jar trying to put the drink into it.

s: Yómetsobaonra nokon nónti bokánke, jaton botín mánexon.
e: The thieves took my canoe and put it into their boat.
Now even bijao leaves are expensive in Pucallpa.

s: Jóni páenara mánipein mápokanke ói béaitian.
e: Since it was raining, they covered a drunk man with a banana leaf.

s: Xobón maníketianra áni níweaban nokon kóka pákeke.
e: When my uncle stood on top of the house, a strong wind made him fall.

s: Maníx meran káketianronki jóni ronón natéxke.
e: They say that when the man went off through the underbrush, a snake bit him.

s: Maníx sénenainra ábion pakéke; kánchis jónira mawáke.
e: When the forest ended, a plane crashed; seven people died.

s: Jatíribi máyoronabora moa maníx meranoax jokónkasai.
e: Some Matsés people now want to leave the jungle.

s: Moa kámpo maníx íketianra, ábion pakéti átipanyamake.
e: Since the field was covered with weeds, the small plane could not land.

s: Moa tsóa pirótanin tsíniamaitianra, moa kámpo maníxke.
e: Since no one played soccer anymore, the field became covered with weeds.

s: Jawen íbo mawáketianra, nato xóbo moa maníxke.
e: After the owner of this house died, this place became forested.
They say that when we eat mangoes it makes us lazy.
They say that if you put pijuayo (peach palm) oil on your hair, you can avoid going bald.

s: Páena jónira manón pakéke, titán jawen chitónti síkati biátonin.
e: A drunk man fell into the black clay that mother had gotten to paint her pampanilla (skirt).

s: Nétetibi mánokoxotira non xétabo ishtón payóyamai.
e: If we rinse our mouths every day, our teeth won't decay so quickly.
Even though we didn't know where he was, we asked around until we found him.

s: Moa mánota ikénbira rabé néte bénaxon nókokanke.
e: He had gotten lost; they searched for him for two days and found him.

s: Non óinabira moa ábion manóke, naíkoin meran.
e: As we watched, the plane disappeared from sight among the clouds.

s: Moa mánsaman piá ikaxa, xéki bánaabi, xóxoyamai.
e: Since moths have attacked the planted corn, it isn't growing.

s: Mánsaman piára jíwi tánoke; jatíribira akáma iki.
e: The weevil attacked the tree, and it dried up; but it hasn't attacked the other trees.

s: Nokon bákera mánshiman kéenyamai, námibichores ákasi.
e: My son doesn't like egg yolk; he only likes to eat meat.

s: Mánxaman kawáti rawéxon xéaaxa nokon chái méchaa iki.
e: My brother-in-law drank the juice from this shrub's scraped bark and became a good fisherman.

s: Manxán pikáshamaira nato báke wíniai, ísores ákasi.
e: This child is crying because he doesn't want to eat heron; he only wants spider monkey.

s: Jónikonbaonra jímimanxan píyamakanai Inkán jimiya íketian.
e: The Shipibo don't eat pink herons, because this heron has the blood of the Inca.

s: Nokon wíso kotonra moa manxányora iki; jákopira en sáweyamai.
e: My black shirt is very faded, and that's why I don't wear it anymore.

s: Béro manxán ikáxa rábini káyamake, kénakanabi.
e: They invited him but he didn't go, because he was ashamed that his eye had turned gray.

s: Nokon tári mechá íketianra en barín manxánhake.
e: I put my wet cushma (tunic) out in the sun.

s: Oín mecháara, moa non chópa chíikan manxánhake.
e: We have already dried by the fire the clothes that the rain had gotten wet.

s: Nokon kotón titán nétetibi barínko akára manxánke.
e: Mother faded my shirt by putting it out in the sun every day.

s: Manxánteon jawen báke kópinaketianra, Korín Nima oínkaxamai bepóke.
e: Korín Nima covered her face so as not to see the jabiru stork near her baby, afraid it would cutipar (cast a harmful spell on) her little one.

s: Jawen chiárexti manxán iketianra rábini jóyamake.
e: He didn't come because he was ashamed of his faded trousers.

s: Kirípininra ea íbirai nokon manxántora isín iki.
e: Maybe I have the flu, because my palate hurts.
**ki jonín káshibo tsákanike manxónbinain.** They say that long ago a man stabbed a Cashibo man in the crown of the head.

s: Kímika yóitima bakénronki maxónbinaki awá tsakánike.
e: They say that long ago three unruly children deliberately struck a sachavaca (tapir) on the crown of its head.

s: Xatéxon máoxen akáronki jakón iki; játian jími bóyamai.
e: They say it is good to put white clay on a cut, to keep the blood from flowing.
This is the map of Peru.

s: Mapáchira jáke Nóriti Amirikain jáinoax Sóro Amirikain. Ja riki jawéki ánima ochítitio. Ikáxbi jawen jínares nenké. Janra píti chókai, pínoxon.
e: The raccoon lives in North America and in South America. It is an animal about the size of a dog, not very large, with a long tail. It washes its food before eating.

s: Oi béaitianra nokon titán chómo en peín mapánke.
e: When it was raining, I covered mother's jar with a bijao leaf.

s: En piaitianra nokon xéta mapekenin ea chexake.
e: When I was eating, my decayed tooth started to hurt.

s: Nato xéatia chómo mápemeeketianra, xóya nanéke.
e: When this jar of drink came uncovered, a mouse got into it.
The metal pot came uncovered because it had so much drink in it.

s: Jawen maríta mapénketianra jawen pátoronin jóni kastíkanke.
e: The boss punished the man because he opened his suitcase.
qui jonín yatánike. They say that when the Inca's servant girl came up out of the water at an angle, a man grabbed her.
When the thief climbed up onto the top of the house, they caught him.

s: Moátianronki iká iki westíora mápijoni, jawen béro chánka.
e: They say that long ago there was a shrimp-man with bulging eyes.

s: Káchio káxonki jóni téxtekaanike; jatian jawen mápobichoki tárameeti jónike.
e: They say that once a man went into the jungle and cut his own throat; only his head came rolling back.

s: Mapó jóniakanaronki tétekan bópaonike, jóni shinánkin.
e: They say that long ago the hawk used to carry off clay figures shaped like people, thinking they were real people.

s: Mapó axón en ícha koríki bikénbira ea yómetsoakanke.
e: I earned a lot of money making pottery, and it was stolen from me.

s: Mapóchekereninra báke xóntako tékake, jánbi méeresaitian.
e: A *mapóchekere* wasp stung a girl because she had disturbed it.

s: Máikini mápotira ea papán yóike, jaín nokon wétsa kánaketian.
e: My father sent me to cover a hole in the ground so my little brother wouldn't fall into it.

s: Chopán janbíx mapóketianra báke jóiman réteke.
e: A baby suffocated when it became covered by a blanket.

s: Yámikenti mapótira báke yóitiman chíiki pótake.
e: The unruly child threw the metal pot's lid into the fire.

s: Níweaba pakéxonra nokon xóbo mapóti pótake.
e: A gust of wind came and tore off the thatch ridge of my house.
The rain soaked us because we had no pamacari (tarp cover).

s: Káchio kaxónra mápoxao non méranike, jóni inón piní.
e: We went into the jungle many years ago and found the skull of a man that a jaguar had devoured.
That gringo is completely bald.
On feast days the soldiers march wearing their leg wrappings.
While building the house, a man fell from the ridge beam.

s: Moátianronkí Marányanimea táshi bípaokanike non rekénbaon.
e: They say that in the old days our ancestors used to go get salt from the Marañón River.
The Cashibo make their arrows with agouti teeth, which serve as blades.

s: Márinirobaon shinánkana iki, moa jabo mái kéxa taxnáti kaí.
e: The sailors thought they were close to land.

s: Jawen maríta mapénketianra, jawen pátoronin jóni kastíkanke.
e: The boss punished the man because he opened his suitcase.
I left after they had finished buying.
The women went to sell their necklaces.
Trying to make a canoe without knowing how, the man ruined it.

s: Nato mikánikora rámakaya áxei ítai; jákopira nokon motóro masáake.
e: This mechanic is just now learning, and he has ruined my motor.
What a job, and so well done!

s: Minbíxa moa mia masáke; jaskápainonra nokon jói min senénhayamake.
e: It's your own fault; you didn't heed my advice.

s: Bóchikiaxbira ábion masáke; jaín páketara onántima iki.
e: The plane broke down in mid-air, and nobody knows where it crashed.

s: Ráo másata shéaasha nato jóni pasná iki.
e: This man is pale from drinking a spoiled herbal remedy.

s: Jawen jakóma shinánya kopira nato jóni masáke.
e: This man has had bad luck because of his evil thoughts.
In the old days they used to forbid touching the huingo, so that one wouldn't go bald.

s: Máshi bépokootaxa nato jóni béro kóroke, ráomeeyamaáx.
e: When sand got into this man's eye, it turned gray and dry because it wasn't treated.
According to the story, while pursuing the Inca, they slept on the beaches three times, and even so they did not catch up with him.
The Coast is a region of Peru.

s: Máshimaxka ikáinra ábion pakéke kásorina kéyotáx.
e: The plane landed on the upper part of the beach when it ran out of gasoline.

s: Chéxeinkanronki jato mashínti onámaa iki, onányamakankenbi.
e: They say that Black Inca made the red clay known to his people, when they still did not know of it.

s: Enra pikín nokon xéta mapeke mashtínke.
e: From eating, my decayed molar started to hurt.

s: rétekasira jóni róme koimán masónike; ikáxbira janbíx paénke.
e: The man blew tobacco smoke on his head, wanting to kill the lice, but he got dizzy.

s: Maspó meran íxonra jonín wísoino rétea iki.
e: From his hiding place a man killed a yanapuma (black jaguar).

s: Jóni mérati jóaitianronki non xobón péyakaax mátataon kéotai.
e: They say the atatai sings perched on our house, as a sign that a visitor is coming.

s: Aínbaon ompáx chomón axón máixon bóaitianra, jawen wetsán mátake.
e: A woman put a jar of water on her head, and while she was carrying it, her sister took it off for her.

s: Mato kámpo bénxoai ítainbira, piróta ákaibo moa nokókanke.
e: While you all were fixing up the field, the soccer players arrived.

s: Maton bánko arós wai áxonara, moa Sinámosnin bíke.
e: The rice field that you all planted for the bank has already been taken by the state agency SINAMOS.

s: Matora koáratianin bénabenai; sontaro iti bononxon jabátankanwe.
e: The guard is looking for you all to enlist you for military service; it would be better if you fled.

s: Mátokameara áni inón jóni bíke, tóoatioma iketian.
e: A large jaguar attacked a man who was on the hill, because he didn't have a shotgun with him.

s: Mátokameaxa jóni yámaaxbi sión ikai; jáskararonki yoshín iki —írakanai.
e: From the top of the hill someone is shouting, but no one can be seen there. They say it is a demon.
Your chief is a very capable man.
They say the *matósh* insect eats buried corpses.

s: Nato oxénra mátsi pakénoxiki; jáskara kopira non károai.
e: This month it will be cold; that's why we'll gather firewood.
The San Juan cold snap is killing me.
My father is crushing ice.
Since I have a fever, I feel cold.

s: Mátsi ikénbira mato ói meranbi jóke.
e: You all have come right in the middle of the rain, and despite the cold.

s: Eara níti bénota iki, mátsi jíkiax.
e: I stopped walking when my rheumatism started.

s: Rókotoronra ea raón matsínke; axónbira ea kóboranyamake.
e: The doctor put drops of medicine on my injured head, and unlike what I expected, didn't charge me for it.

s: Ia ícha ikaxra nokon títa mátsokasai; jákopira náshii kake.
e: My mother's head itches because she has so many lice; that's why she has gone to bathe.

s: Ia ícha ikaxra, nokon títa mátsoai.
e: My mother is rubbing her head because she has so many lice.

s: Inkan áwinin mátsotaitianronki béskoman chíi bónike.
e: They say that while the Inca's wife was sweeping, the little chirriclés parrot carried off a burning ember.
chíi bóaitianronki matsótinin ríshkinike. They say that when the little chirriclés parrot was carrying off fire, the Inca's wife hit it with the broom.
From running so much, this child fell fainted and lost consciousness.

s: Kétokanra mawábo píkoa iki, Kakónkonia pántionhaiona.
e: The riverbank collapse uncovered corpses from the Caco cemetery, which was located at the edge of the river.

s: Bákeronki mawánki tíiatima iki; játianronki máwatai.
e: They say one must not touch a baby on the fontanelle, because then it could die.

s: Non íno kéotai máwaketianronki noa bíti iki.
e: They say that when we imitate a jaguar roaring, it can attack us.
Imitate what I do.

s: Nato jónira máwamis iki; jáskatira ishtón ásheai.
e: This man is a good mimic; no wonder he learns quickly.

s: Nato jonín xóbora jakónhira iki; rámara já mawá énribi anóxiki.
e: This man's house is very beautiful; now I too will try to make one just like it.
They say that when we encounter a ghost, we can faint.

s: Rókotoronra mawátibishoko jóni ráonai; bénxoti jisáma riki.
e: The doctor is treating a person who is about to die; but it seems there is no hope of recovery.

s: Jíria íketianra noa jóniki rakéyamai; moa máwata íketianresa noa ráketai.
e: When someone is alive, we are not afraid of them; but when they are dead, we are.

s: Jónibora bári mawáketian rakeérakebaini risánti xobón bokánke, jaton báchi iábaini.
e: Once when there was a solar eclipse, some people went to the church frightened, carrying their mosquito nets.

s: Nokon títashokonra westíora máwetan ákai, kírínkonin yónoa.
e: My grandmother is making a *máwetan* jar because a gringo commissioned it from her.

s: Ajíntininra non jéma máweti noa yóike moa píshta sénenaitian.
e: The municipal agent told us to rake our yards because the festival was approaching.

s: Ríkatoninra máweti ícha bóai, ikáxbira kopíora iki; jáskara ikénra en jíwibi ákai.
e: The traveling trader carries many rakes for sale, but they are very expensive; so, I will make my own out of wood.

s: Nato jonín kanóti mawékasara risbí teséke.
e: The cord broke as this man tried to string the crossbow.
Pedro is taller than José.

s: Moátianronki chaxónki manánxawe íshtokin mawínti átipanyamaiki.
e: They say that long ago the deer could not beat the tortoise in a race.
They say that long ago the tapir used to fish with a sitarákuy pincer, which it used as a fishhook.
They say they brought gravel from the San Alejandro River.

s: Nato kámpaainbora maxén beskíke, jáskati áxea ikáx.
e: This Campa woman crushed annatto to paint her face, doing it like this with annatto, according to the tribe's custom.
deck of a steamship

s: Jawen yóra páxnaxoko ikáxbi íxtoxonra jonín máxkabainke.
e: Running with a weak body, the man fainted.
The woman fainted while giving birth to a large baby.

s: Moa máxkaa rabé óra wínota pekaora mia jóke. Moácha joxónra min jíria nókokeanke.
e: You have come two hours after he expired; if you had come a little sooner, you would have still found him alive.
He just expired tonight, and tomorrow they will bury him.

s: Apónra noa koríki ménike ískoira xóboati; ikáxbira máxkatai.
e: The government gave us money to build the school, but it's going to fall short anyway.

s: Ja misiónma noa jawékiati méniara jatíribibo máxkáke.
e: Some of us were short of the provisions the mission distributed to us.

s: Ea máxko íketianra, nokon papán íno reteaiki.
e: When I was small, my father killed a jaguar.
Young people nowadays don't get their hair cut.
That short-haired man fell from the truck.
They say that long ago the motelo (tortoise) caused the opossum to die of hunger.

s: Nato bákera wetsa bakén maxónakai, jawen wetsán máshi mápota.
e: One child blows on another's head because his brother put sand on it.

s: Báke maxpora jawen titán nanén mápoki ákai, bóo nenké benón ixon.
e: The mother puts huito on her baby's head, which has fine little hairs, so that its hair will grow long.

s: Tamánya chichóra kikínbires mayá ícha iki; jénetianra jáskarama iki.
e: The Tamaya River has very many bends in the dry season, but not in the rainy season.

s: Chósko mayá pekao yáwa nónoaira non nókoyantanke.
e: Four bends later, we came across white-lipped peccaries swimming.

s: Min máyaara nato aínbaon kinánke, beyóskiranxon.
e: This woman vomited because she got dizzy when you spun her around.

s: Nato xóbo máyakinra en mérayamake, mawákin nokon epán koríki míina.
e: Even though I went around this house, I didn't find the money my late uncle had buried.

s: Nato mái máyatainbira non onányamake ániora íketian.
e: Even though the earth is spinning, we don't notice it because it is so huge.

s: Onányamax káxa ea mayáke bénotax; jákopira ea ixtón jóyamake.
e: I went off without knowing the way, got lost, and wandered around in circles; that's why I couldn't get back quickly.

s: Rámara moa máyobo ráea iki; jatíribira Yarínain békana iki.
e: Now some Matsés are already civilized, and some have come to Yarina.
to wash one's hands
without fingers
to cut the nails of
lump on the wrist
with bushy hair on the front legs
insect legs
to gather (fruit) from the outer branches
a fringe of finger-shaped cords hung from something as an ornament
He is from the village.
He has come from the oxbow lake.

s: Jíwi mebi xátexonra, bái napon papán meánhake chóshinon ixon.
e: Father cut the outer branches of the tree and spread them out on the path so they would dry.

s: Moa meántires ikénbira jéne bexón mánkoa réteke.
e: When this mango tree was about to become leafy, the flood came and dried it out.
The tuyuyo (stork) nests and hatches its young in trees that grow leafy.

s: Jonínronki jawen mébibo yamín xátekin kéyonike, jíwi xátekin.
e: They say that long ago a man cut off all his fingers with the axe while cutting a tree.

s: Jiwín néetash penixon mébi sékeaxa bákeranon pakéke.
e: While climbing a tree, the young man stood on the twigs, broke them, and fell to the ground.
This young lady is afraid of the spider's legs.
They say that in the old days they used to marry their daughters to men who were good fishermen.

s: Bári ishtón xánayamaketianra non chópa mechábi sáweke.
e: We put on our clothes still damp, because the sun hadn't come out.

s: Jawen titán jaskáatima yóiabira nato aínbaon jawen chitónti mecháake.
e: This little woman got her pampanilla (skirt) wet, even though her mother had forbidden it.

s: Kámpo mecháma iketianra ábion pakéke non jemán.
e: When the airstrip was dry, the small plane landed in our village.
A man drank an herbal remedy to become a good hunter, and he died.

s: Páronapon réokootaxa non játibi chópabo méchata iki.
e: All our clothes got wet when we capsized in the middle of the river.

s: Enra jasín tsákakin kéneke, wétsaorires méchixon.
e: I shot my arrow at the paují (curassow), but I missed, shooting off in the wrong direction.

s: Noa mécho iketian osánkanaronki sinátima iki.
e: They say that if someone laughs at us for being inexperienced, we should not get angry.

s: Papánra jawen báke mécho ímake jawéki ámakashamaxon.
e: This boy doesn't know how to do things well, because his father never demanded that he work.

s: Moátianra nato jóni nóntiati onán ikátiai; rámara moa méchoke bási áyamax.
e: Before, this man was an expert at making canoes, but now he has become out of practice from not having done it in a long time.
The mother washed her child's hands.
In that way the child saved himself.

s: Titára jawen pokónko méekaake, tóoyara íbirai ixon onánox.
e: The mother touched her own belly to find out whether she was pregnant.

s: Jáwebi méeyamawe; noara wétsa jonín xobón iki.
e: Don't touch anything; we're in someone else's house.
Please don't do anything to me.

s: Yobénoxon ónanai jónira masá méeti ónisai jatibi jawekiati, átipanyamax jakopira yobeti atipa yamake.
e: The apprentice becomes sad from depriving himself of food for a long time, and yet he still cannot become a shaman.

s: Chéxeinkanronki jato áxeaa iki, méi betan mapó méskoti.
e: They say that Black Inca taught the people how to mix apacharama bark with clay.

s: Mapó méinkonama ikénbi chómoaara básiamai tóetai.
e: When a large jar is made from clay that is not well mixed with apacharama bark, it doesn't take long to break.

s: Mapóronki ixonra, nato aínbaon mánores meíke, yamé íketian.
e: Thinking it was clay, this woman put her hand into the mud, because it was very dark.

s: Nato bakénra mékayao pikáshamakin mémiores píai.
e: This child wants to eat with his left hand, not with his right.

s: Káchio káxa, bái mekayao káx nokon épa benóke.
e: My uncle went into the jungle and got lost by going to the right of the path.

s: Jawen mekémapokira nato báke binán tékake, yatánketian.
e: The wasp stung this child on the thumb when he grabbed it.

s: Nato jónira mekémebi nenkébo iki, jaskábi píkota ikax.
e: This man has long fingers, born that way.
A man died when a jergón (fer-de-lance snake) bit him on the back of the hand.

s: Nokon mékayaó mekén jaínxon nokon mémiokea mekénra óinke.
e: He looked at my right hand, and then at my left.

s: Yómetso jónira mekén xátenaankanke, koríki icha bíketian.
e: The thief had his hand cut off for stealing a lot of money.

s: Jóninra jawen rayós mekén tónkoaxon tímake paénxon.
e: A drunk man made a fist and punched his father-in-law.
**pax wáchoshoko iki.** They say that some people have very soft palms.

s: Oroaitianra jóni ronón natéxke jawen mekénchinitain.
e: While farming, the man was bitten by a snake on his little finger.

s: Kirínko bakera, mekéntechapain jawen ochítininbi natéxke.
e: A young gringo boy was bitten between his fingers by his own dog.
I'm rationing sugar because there's little of it.

s: Asókaro titán mékea ikénbira, báke yoitiman kéyonaanke.
e: The disobedient child finished off all the sugar that mother had jealously been saving.

s: Nato jonínra jatíbitian jawen jawékibo mékeai.
e: This man always keeps his belongings in good condition.

s: Sarámpinin báke íketianra titán jawen báke mékeai.
e: The mother watches jealously over her child when he has measles.

s: Jonínra jawen báke pikóketian mékekin xóno xáteyamai kópinaketian.
e: When a son is born, the man protects him and doesn't cut lupuna (kapok tree), for fear of cutipar-ing (casting a harmful spell on) his little son.
When we go looking for mitayo (game meat), we become cunning.
They say that when one drinks piripiri (a medicinal plant) to become a good fisherman, one must perform rites of abstinence.
This man has been fasting inside the mosquito net for two days.

s: Mékexeeyara natéxmisma iki; ikáxbira jawen mekénhain itan taénko mókaya iki.
e: The salamanca doesn't bite, but it has venom in its front and hind feet.

s: Mékexoyara xánbo jisáribi iki; ikáxbi jawen jína nenkéma iki.
e: The salamander looks very much like a lizard, but has a short tail.
A woman from Caco was killed by a salamanca.

s: Ochítinin natéxketianra nato báke rókotoron mekéxke.
e: When a dog bit the fingers of this child, the doctor stitched them up.
She burned her hand in the fire.

s: Nato baín káx mémio bái ikátonin katánwe; ján riki min pápa.
e: Going along this path, turn in on the left; that's where your father is.
Stay to my left so that it doesn't grab you.
The motor sank on the left bank of the river.
Go quickly to the house.

s: Moa píshta ikáinra ea joménke, jawékiatibo beí.
e: Since the feast is already approaching, I came ahead of time, bringing provisions.
The child is biting his own hand.
The child's own brother is biting his hand.

s: Rímameaxa jóni móromenexetin ménexeeya jóke; jáskara ikénra Ínka shinánkanke.
e: A man came from Lima wearing beaded bracelets, and because of that they thought he was the Inca.

s: Chíchika ménikanon ishon jato yóiabira tsónbi pápa méniamake; játianra moa janbíx ménikaake.
e: Father insisted that they give him the knife, but no one gave it to him; finally he took it himself.
A talented woman knows how to make designs.

s: Ichaakin wastén raónxonra, titán jawen báke menínhake.
e: By treating her many times with piripiri (a medicinal plant), the mother made her daughter into an artist.

s: Rámara ea moa menínke wétsabaon jawéki aká máwaax.
e: I finally became an artist, by copying what others do.

s: Pátoroninra jawen jónibo koríki ménike, xonón téekanon ishon.
e: The boss gave his workers money as an advance so they would go cut lupuna (kapok trees).

s: Jáwenama ikénbira nato aínbo chopán ménitai; rámara jawen íbo sínatai.
e: This woman is handing out clothing that isn't hers; her owner might get angry.

s: Nokon nonón menkó ikénbira nokon papán pátoronin bóke.
e: My father's boss took my egg-laying duck.

s: Atapa menkokanra píamai, moa ísiman yátana ixon.
e: The broody hen doesn't want to eat, because the plague has taken hold of her.

s: Titán jawen átapa menkómakenbira ochítinin jawen báchibo tóshamake.
e: Mother set her hen to brood, but the dog made it break its eggs.

s: Titán kentí ménkonara kochín páke, íshtoi kakín.
e: Running past, the pig knocked over the pot that mother had set upside down.

s: Nónti ménkota ikáinkora, yáwa ina iki, káchiokea beá.
e: In the place where the canoe is turned face down, there is a young collared peccary, brought from the jungle.
The tired man lay down face down, already exhausted.
Last night the brooding hen was carried off by the ocelot.

s: Moa wái menó ikénbi átsa bánayamaara moa náwea iki.
e: Even though the field had already been burned, they didn't plant manioc, and it turned into purma (fallow secondary growth).

s: Wái ménokinra manánxawe píchika bikánke, wétsa moa méxota.
e: While burning the field, they caught five motelos (tortoises), one of them already charred.

s: Nokon xóbora kéyo ménoke nokon ráwikan.
e: My enemy burned down and completely destroyed my house.
The man who got burned was taken to the hospital.

s: Jóni mentsís nenkéra Kakónko nokóke, néte máyai jóai.
e: A man with long fingernails, who was going around circling the world, arrived at Caco.

s: Westíora jónira yómetsoketian jawen táementsis tsekákanke.
e: They tore out the toenails of a certain man who had stolen.

s: Nato aínbora meósoti sáweisma iki; jákopira rábinai.
e: This woman never wears a ring, and so she feels ashamed.

s: Non ashé riki, yósibaon píainko báke ikax mépitima.
e: It is our custom that children not eat together with grown men.
Where the slope of the hill ends, there is gold.

s: Jonínra ea máshi mepóke en asókaro yókata; jakóma shinánya ixon.
e: A mean man threw a handful of sand at my hand when I asked him for sugar.
Upon being discovered in adultery, the woman hid.
The woman discovered in adultery was cast off by her husband.
Upon being discovered in adultery, the man fled.

s: Nokon wetsán ríkara bórosa meran iki.
e: My brother's cast net is inside the bag.
They caught the thief when he entered the house.

s: Pátorónin tapánra Xawánya táe meran íki.
e: The boss's raft is inside the Shahuaya stream.

s: Empari méraketianra, nokon wetsán róno mérashokoke.
e: When I had already found the fer-de-lance, my brother saw it too.

s: Ochokeabira nokon pápa jóaitian en mérake.
e: From far away I caught sight of my father coming.

s: Moa merá íketian nínkataxa ea ratéke.
e: Hearing that I had already been found, I was astonished.

s: Nato aínbaonra jawen benén mérati bachínke.
e: This woman pulled the hair of her husband's lover.

s: Mérati kakénbi tsón bíamaara noa jóke.
e: We went to visit them, but no one received us, so we came back.

s: Meráyan tárironki inín iki, béroyoshinbo betan yóyo iti kopi.
e: They say that shamans' magical cushmas (tunics) are perfumed so that they can thereby speak with the spirits.
When this man got sick, his hand shriveled up.

s: Jóni méshakonti shínanira pápashoko jéne meran káke.
e: While trying to greet a man, the old grandfather fell into the water.

s: Méshi bénakinra káchiokea titán íno mérake.
e: While looking for dry twigs, mother came across a jaguar in the jungle.
The child was stung by wasps while burning the dry branches.

s: Nato joníra áni ikaxbi méshishoko iki.
e: This man is tall, but very slender.
The *méshipapi* caterpillar eats leaves.
The manioc my mother roasted got burned.
When the gasoline caught fire, it charred two men.

s: Moa méshotainbira en mia kóma bótéxonke
e: I took the panguana (a bird) off the fire for you, because it was about to burn.

s: Meshóbira ákai nato aínbaon pikín, yoáati onáma
e: **íxon**. This woman always eats burnt food because she doesn't know how to cook.
Two cars became charred after crashing into each other.
The children are getting their hands and faces stained.

s: Asókaro betan táxi meskóta ikénbira onányamaxon nato bakén Xéake.
e: This child swallowed sugar mixed with salt without realizing it.
Yesterday various different people marched in the feast.
Fish soup mixed with chili pepper is delicious.

s: Mapó betan méi méskoshon chómoaaronki bási íkai.
e: They say that a jar made from clay mixed with apacharama bark lasts a long time.
At last the oil mixed with the water.

s: Rámara kónibo jónibo moa kámpabo betan méskotai.
e: Now the Konibo are mixing with the Campa.

s: Joshín joé betan jósho joéra méskoti metsáshaman iki.
e: It's very pretty when the red light turns to white and vice versa.

s: Rabé mesó xéki bérora ea jonín ménike.
e: A man gave me two handfuls of dry corn.

s: Méstiira nato aínbo ábionin kaí betíke.
e: This woman closed her eyes while traveling on the plane, because she was afraid.

s: Bákera wíniwiniai, jiwín néeketian jawen wetsán shákona méstii pakenaketian.
e: The child is crying because his older brother is shaking the tree he has climbed, and he's afraid of falling.
The dog is eating the food that fell from mom's hand.

s: Ishto kakínra en títa píti métake.
e: By passing by quickly, I made the food fall from mom's hand.
They cut off the thief's wrist.

s: Nokon chiárextira moa kímisha báritiaya iki; jákopira moa métexeekai.
e: My pants are already three years old, and that's why they're already falling apart.
By accident, the woman spilled the porridge while serving it.

s: Píti métexara kóchi betan ochítininres píke.
e: Only the pig and the dog ate the food that was served.
crumbs of food fallen from the hand
This crazy man points at himself.
They say that if we point at the rainbow, sores can appear on our fingers.

s: Timaanankinra nato bákeranoman jawen métoti sékeke.
e: In a fistfight this young man broke his index finger.

s: Naránxa bimi ícha íibatara moa metókana iki.
e: Yesterday there were many oranges, but they have already been picked.
Your design is very beautiful.
Your sister is extremely pretty.
**rókotoron pápa ráo xéamake.** The doctor gave my dad medicine to drink because he was moaning from a headache.

s: Méwemeara nokon epán sókota jóno réteke wetsánra witáxki natéxke.
e: My uncle killed six collared peccaries at a salt lick, and one of them bit him on the leg.
A thief took all the money this child had in his hand.

s: Nato bákera méwexeetai, jawen mentsís nenkéira ikáx.
e: This child scratches himself with his hand because his fingernails are very long.

s: Iso rétexon méxaitianra jóni inábaon yatánke.
e: While the man was pulling out the fur of the spider monkey he had killed, wild Indians captured him.
Dad brought a live pucacunga (a trumpeter bird) after plucking its feathers.

s: Moa kári méxashon béaitianra en nókoke.
e: I found him already bringing the sweet potatoes he had pulled up from the ground.

s: Nokon wétsara en átsa mexa bíti ráanai waínko.
e: I send my brother to the garden to bring back the pulled-up yuca.
A paiche (a giant Amazon fish) broke the cord binding of my harpoon.
The fallen bristles of the pig are in the middle of the path.

s: Moa básiora ikaxa nato íno bichi méxetai.
e: The little hairs of this old jaguar hide are falling out.

s: Nato átapa ranira méxetai, moa máwata ikax.
e: The little feathers of this hen are falling out because it is dead.
The planted plantains uprooted themselves.

s: Méxka ixonra nato aínbaon jawen báke rerake.
e: Because she is left-handed, this woman cut her son.

s: Kampónra kímisha aínbo charóke. Ja méxkao iká riki nokon pói.
e: Three women are standing on the sports field. The one on the left is my sister.

s: Jawen axé íketianra nato bakén jawen méxkao wíshai.
e: This child writes with his left hand out of habit.

s: Weán méxkaokea iká kínira wíso inon kíni iki.
e: To the left of the stream there is a hole that is the den of a yanapuma (a mythical black jaguar).
This crawling baby fell off the emponado (a split-palm-wood floor platform).

s: Yamín jawen táe xáteaxa nokon kóka méxomexokirani jóke.
e: My uncle came crawling because he cut his foot with an axe.
The girl cut her hand after scraping her arm.

s: Nokon chaínra, nónti ishtón jankénhake, meyáyora íshon.
e: My brother-in-law finished making the canoe in a short time because he is very skillful.

s: Nokon cháibichora meyá iki; wétsabora jáskarama iki.
e: Only my brother-in-law is skillful; the others are not.
to spit

s: Mía riki jakóma jóni; jákopira en mia kastíkanai —akinra tiníntinin jóni áke.
e: The lieutenant governor said to the man: —You are a bad person, and that is why I am going to punish you.

s: Mia jákoni téetaitianra en senén kopíai —ikira pátoron íke.
e: The boss said: —If you work well, I will pay you fairly.

s: Min shobo ákaitianra en mia akíntiki, nokon rárebo mia íketianres.
e: When you build the house, I will help you; but only because you are my relative.

s: Nokon wétsa min kastíkanaitianra, en mia koáratiaiba bóai.
e: If you punish my brother, I am going to take it to the guard.

s: Máio shiainxonra en mia óina iki; ixónbira en mia onányamaa iki.
e: I saw you in Pucallpa, but I didn't know you.

s: Jonínra oránshin xéaxonbi míchoke, béxnaman kéenkin.
e: The man spat out the soda again after tasting it; he prefers liquor.

s: Moátianronki maxóki inón párana míimeeta iki.
e: They say that long ago the fox buried itself alive, tricked by the jaguar.
They say that after falling from a height, it buried itself in the mud.

s: Mawá míinabora jatíbi kétokan píkoa iki.
e: All the buried corpses turned up in the cemetery because of the landslide.

s: Nato mikánikora rámakaya áxei ítai; jákopira nokon mótoro masáake.
e: This mechanic is still learning; that's why he has ruined my motor (outboard motor).
The fox took your hen.

s: Otokoronkonia jónira mínka áti chániti joke.
e: A man from Utucuro came to invite us to a minga.
One hour has sixty minutes.
hour hand, minute hand
Not knowing how to prepare it, my mom made the porridge lumpy.

s: Keyón mintonronki yobébaon jato xéamai, jáboribi yobé ítiakin.
e: They say that shamans make their students swallow little balls of saliva so that they too will become shamans.

s: Atsa mintonra nato bakén nákaamabi píke.
e: This child swallowed the little balls made of yuca without chewing them.

s: Yobébaonra keyón mintónhaxon jato óyoai, ja ísinaibo.
e: Shamans form little balls of saliva to suck on the skin of the sick, thereby healing them.
While mom is preparing the food, she eats the lumps.
When a snake is coiled up, it means it is ready to bite anyone.

s: Róno míntona en tíakabira ea nateshamake, óxaa ixon.
e: I touched a coiled-up snake and it didn't bite me because it was asleep.
I am going to the market to shop.

s: Nokon báke ísinaitianra míriko bénati ea yóikanaiki.
e: When my son got sick, they told me I should go find a healer.
half a liter
From eating melon, the child got diarrhea.
They've already caught the murderer
Now the guards are catching them one after another.
The child fell asleep and fell off the table.
The flood killed all the kittens.
The cat is the dog's enemy.
They say that if you suck on cane syrup, you become lazy.
I caught a gymnotid eel with a hook.
Nima is fishing for sardines with a hook for his little brother.
**iki.** All the fish that I've brought have been caught with a hook.
The boy threw away his grandfather's fishhook.
In Yarina a child died after choking on a bone stuck in his throat.
The child got hooked by a fishhook.
This man has never eaten tamales.

s: Moa pishta íti ochómara aínbaon misiai.
e: The woman is preparing humitas because the feast is approaching.

s: Misiónma noa jawékiati méniara jatíribibo maxkáke.
e: Some of us have run short of the provisions that the mission distributed to us.

s: Misionirobora jaton rárebo jénebeirani Piróri békana iki.
e: The missionaries came to Peru, leaving their relatives behind.

s: Axo yoshinronki jawen ponyán mískobires iki.
e: They say the demon of the capirona tree has knotted, twisted branches for arms.
A shaman died of cramps.
They say that in Iparía there is an illness that causes cramps.
Because he had been running, the man got cramps and died.
They say that when we touch something belonging to the Cashibo, we get cramps.

s: Mispán akinra atsa xákixon peín kawati iki.
e: Yuca tamales are prepared by grating the yuca and wrapping it in a plantain leaf.
A while ago, mom prepared yuca tamales because dad likes them.

s: Ráma mitán nete ikénra, manón síkaanankanai.
e: Since today is Carnival day, people get themselves dirty painting themselves with mud.
I don't like playing at Carnival.

s: Noara jákiribi joríbai mitán iti ochóma.
e: We're going to go back because Carnival time is coming around again.

s: Píchika mítoroyara nokon nónti en ákai.
e: I am making my canoe five meters long.

s: Nokon konxán xatera chósko mítoro iki jawen nenké.
e: My cedar log is four meters long.

s: Mítoro yámaketianra noa konxán pátoronin topónxonyamake.
e: Since there was no meter stick, the boss didn't measure our cedar lumber.
Bundles of merchandise arrived from Lima.

s: Pápara jawen pátoronin chópa mixe bexónke.
e: Dad's boss brought him a package of clothes.

s: Titán waxmen mixe ikainra xoyán náake.
e: A rat made its nest in the ball of cotton that mom had bundled up.

s: Titán yomán mixera jawen bakén ménonaanke.
e: The child burned his mom's ball of thread.
Rats don't eat the cotton when it is packaged.
I have already settled the matter.
They say our ancestors were fierce.

s: Janra moa máxkake. Moácha joxonra, min jíria nókokeanke.
e: He has already died. If you had come a little earlier, you would have found him alive.

s: Moátianra noa Otokoronko ikátiai; rámara moa noa Kakónko iki.
e: Long ago we lived in Utucuro, but now we live in Caco.
In ancient times we were ignorant.
They say that in ancient times the Incas lived in this region.

s: Moáxeniora bikana ikaxa nato motóro básimashokobo másatai.
e: This motor keeps breaking down because it's very old.
The old-time boats didn't have motors.

s: Mócho piáxa nato aínbo jími chixóke.
e: From eating turushuque, this woman had bloody diarrhea.
This disobedient child isn't afraid of ishanga (stinging nettle).
The child doesn't cry even though his mother whips him with ishanga.
They say the jaguar cracks its tail but doesn't break it.
The chief drank the very fermented masato.

s: Kikínbires móka ikénbira papán naránxa kókoke.
e: Dad ate the orange even though it was very sour.
From eating a bitter lemon, the little child got a canker sore.
This medicine is bitter.

s: Bóe tashínaka móka piáxa ea nómiai.
e: I ate a very salty boquichico (a river fish) and I'm thirsty.

s: Yóchi móka axónra nato bakén asókaro kókoke.
e: After eating very spicy chili pepper, this child ate sugar to calm the spiciness.
The bite of the fer-de-lance is the most painful of all.
Since the sun was very strong, we kept bathing throughout the trip.
The strength of the salt makes clothing disintegrate quickly.

s: Táwi móka keskara en xéake jonín ámaa.
e: A man made me drink something like bile.
He coated his blowgun dart with poison.

s: Píshtatian xéanoxonra, Charáxmanan jónibaon jatíbitian xéati mókaai.
e: The people of Charashmaná always ferment the drink heavily for feasts.
They say that in a future war the foreigners will surely poison the air, killing everyone.
A child fathered by the demon of the *mókapari* tree turns out to be a good hunter and fisherman.
When I suck on an orange that has turned sour, it makes me dizzy.

s: Moa chícha mókaketianra jónibo páenax tímaanankanai.
e: When the chicha turns bitter and fermented, people get drunk and fight.

s: Nato aínbaonra yoáati onányamabirake; jákopira píti betén táshi mókaake.
e: Maybe this woman doesn't know how to cook, and that's why her fish chowder is too salty.

s: Sibóriaya méskoara moa kikínbires yóchi mókake.
e: The chili pepper mixed with onion turned very spicy.

s: Bári mókaketianra nato jonín kinánke, jawen yóra ísinai iken.
e: When the sun turned strong, this man vomited because he was ill.

s: Nato bakénra konjíti mókoke, jawen titán jishnóma
e: This child put a candy in his mouth without his mother seeing.

s: Aínbaonra píti mokobi jawen báke pímake.
e: A woman fed her little child the same food she had in her mouth.
They say that if we eat *mómo* fish, we can go bald.
By running, the horse made the ground sink.

s: Yámikenti mónaketianra, titán nokon wétsa ríshkike.
e: Mom whipped my brother for having dented the metal pot.
The girl wrapped the doll in a cloth.
With the earthquake, the ground sank in and a person was swallowed and buried.
—iquira títa íke. Mom said: —I don't want this dented pot.

s: Anixobo ménotainkora, morínchopa kéyoti ménota iki.
e: In the store that burned down, the "morín" cloth was burned up.
They say that in Iquitos trade beads are cheap.
To multiply is with "x".
A man wants a beaded necklace.

s: Koáratianinra jóni ríshkixon jawen xáo móshake.
e: The guard broke a man's bones by hitting him with a stick.

s: Jawen chómobo moshábo iketianra titán jawen bákebo sináake.
e: Mom scolded her children because their clay jars were cracked.

s: Nato átapa bachi moshábora namán kopíabo márokanai.
e: They are selling these cracked eggs at a low price.

s: Titán básiora chómo ménoara, moa móshiora íke.
e: The clay pot that mom left on the fire for a long time became very brittle.

s: Nokon títashokonra moshí jawékires píai, xétaoma ixon.
e: My grandmother eats only mashed things, since she has no teeth.

s: Pátoroninra páan moshibo jato méniresai, moa kéenyamai.
e: The boss is giving away crumbled bread to the children, since he no longer wants it.

s: Máioshiainoa páan békanara moa móshike, barín aká.
e: The bread they brought from Pucallpa dried out and crumbled because the sun hit it.

s: Jíwibochikiash páketira makánki chóshiti báke sháo moshíke.
e: Falling from up in a tree, the child hit a rock and broke a bone.

s: Nato kémpo móshita ikénra ea póntekanke en akáma ikénbi.
e: They blamed me when they found the shattered mocahuas (clay bowls), even though I hadn't done it.

s: Nato jónira móti pikáshamai, tobánres ákasi.
e: This man doesn't like to eat mote; he prefers to eat toasted corn.

s: Nokon átapara móto xéaketian jóiman réteke.
e: When my hen swallowed a ladybug, it died of suffocation.

s: Titán móto aka píkasira báke wíniai.
e: The child is crying because he wants to eat the toasted, ground corn that mother prepared.

s: Westíora motórora réboki káke, téetaibo jawékiati bóxoni.
e: A certain motorboat went upriver carrying supplies for the workers.

s: Rámara moa Máioshiain motórobo kopíora iki.
e: Nowadays in Pucallpa motors are very expensive.

s: Parántajoshinra en mótsake, ján cháchiti yámaketian.
e: I crushed the ripe plantains because I had nothing to mash them with.

s: Atsa joa titán mótsaketianra pápa já xéakashamai.
e: Papa doesn't want to drink the boiled manioc that mama crushed in water.
Sorcerers are afraid to drink things crushed in water and prepared by someone else, because they fear it will harm them.
Dad's foot swelled up when he stepped on a tree thorn.
I make noise biting into a raw chili pepper.
When dad bit into a raw yuca, it crunched.

s: Ronón ewan pekáronki móxikai non jámata.
e: They say the boa's back crunches if we step on it.
Now in Pucallpa they make paper from topa wood.
medicine, to treat (make) with medicine
to sleep, to make sleep
head
My head hurts.

to take out from inside
to throw (a spear or arrow) into the water to spear fish
